messages:
sarah_support: FYI customer cust_842 (acct redwood-proj-842) reports large reserved GPU hours on invoice but almost no token usage. Invoice INV-2026-0458 shows 62.3 reserved GPU hours charged for period; console dedicated pool shows ~8.1h. Customer says token count ~1.2k for same window. Can we triage?

miguel_billing: Ack. Can you paste the invoice line and pool id / billing window? Any quick repro steps or screenshots? :eyes:

sarah_support: Invoice line: "Dedicated - reserved GPU hours" qty 62.3, period 2026-05-01 to 2026-05-02. Pool id in dashboard: pool-842 (us-west2). Dashboard hourly meter export attached — shows spikes around 03:10 UTC but total ~8.1h. Customer says they didn't run jobs overnight.

james_infra: Could be warmup churn or instance restart loop. Metering historically counts instance uptime per start event; if instances restart quickly we can inflate billed hours. Can you pull allocation events for pool-842 for that window?

sarah_support: Ran quick export: allocation events CSV attached. Shows many `instance.start` events clustered at 2026-05-01T03:10:12 -> 03:13:00 for 58 distinct lines. No corresponding heavy token traffic in API logs.

anne_cs: Customer is enterprise with SLA. They're asking for an immediate credit while you investigate — can we provisionally apply one?

miguel_billing: I started a billing thread. Initial hypothesis: warmup/auto-scale retries were double-counted into reserved-hour billing. Also check burst/fallback routing — if requests hit hosted fallback, billing attribution could be split. @deploy-bot can you fetch orchestration events for pool-842 in that hour?

deploy-bot: Orchestrator events for pool-842 (2026-05-01T03:00Z -> 2026-05-01T04:00Z):
```
2026-05-01T03:09:58Z instance.create id=inst-842-a
2026-05-01T03:10:02Z instance.start id=inst-842-a
2026-05-01T03:10:07Z instance.create id=inst-842-b
2026-05-01T03:10:10Z instance.start id=inst-842-b
2026-05-01T03:10:12Z instance.start id=inst-842-a  # duplicate start
2026-05-01T03:11:00Z instance.oom id=inst-842-b
2026-05-01T03:11:05Z instance.restart id=inst-842-b
2026-05-01T03:12:30Z instance.start id=inst-842-b  # repeated
...
```
Full dump attached to billing ticket.

james_infra: That pattern looks like a retry loop in the autoscaler/warmup hook. If metering counts each start as billable partial hour without deduping by instance UUID + billing window, it can multiply hours. Quick check: run metering query aggregating unique instance ids rather than start events. Query suggestion:
```
SELECT count(DISTINCT instance_uuid) as instances, SUM(duration_hours) as gpu_hours
FROM instance_metering
WHERE pool_id='pool-842' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-05-01T00:00:00Z' AND '2026-05-02T00:00:00Z'
```
I'll run it now.

miguel_billing: Sounds right. Also check if dedicated reserved hours are charged per allocation request id (which may have been duplicated by the orchestrator). If both metering and billing ingest the same raw stream but with different dedupe keys we can get divergence vs dashboard.

james_infra: Query result: unique instances 4, billed gpu_hours by naive-start-count = 62.3h, deduped-uuid-hours = 7.9h. So metering ingestion double-counted repeated start events as separate billable units. Root cause: autoscaler retries emitted duplicate `instance.start` events without stable UUID for ~58 of those entries. I've opened infra ticket INFRA-901 and pushed a hotfix to debounce start events (PR #3456).

miguel_billing: Thanks. For customer's asked remedy: propose provisional credit for the delta (62.3 - 7.9 = 54.4h). I'll create invoice adjustment request and mark it provisional pending a full retally. Any objections?

anne_cs: Customer is OK with provisional credit. Please mark communication in the ticket and add SLA credit check.

miguel_billing: Created billing ticket BILL-2137, provisional credit requested 54.4 GPU-hours. Also flagged for SLA credit evaluation. Finance notified.

james_infra: Next infra steps: 1) backfill dedup logic in metering ingestion to use instance_uuid as dedupe key for billing windows, 2) deploy autoscaler debounce (PR merged to canary), 3) run a retally job for pool-842 and produce corrected invoice lines. I'll post retally job id when queued.

finance-bot: Noted BILL-2137. Provisional credit approved up to 60 GPU-hours for enterprise account cust_842 pending final retally.

sarah_support: Updated customer: provisional credit & high-priority investigation. They appreciate the quick response. Will keep them updated. :pray:

miguel_billing: Closing loop here once retally completes and invoice is adjusted. Thanks team, great catch on the duplicate start events.

james_infra: Follow-ups: I'll attach logs, PR links, and retally results to INFRA-901 and BILL-2137. If anyone wants the raw CSV I exported, ping me. :thumbsup:
